text:
alex: RFC draft for a new synthetic traffic generator focused on KV cold->warm transitions and kernel-selection parity. Goal: consistent apples-to-apples perf comparisons while reproducing microbursts + long-tail SLO pressure.

maria: sounds useful. important constraint: per-shard warmup windows or batching will hide KV cold misses. we need explicit warmup and measurable probe phases. :+1:

deepak: agree. also we must be able to pin kernels and toggle quant flags in the harness. autotuner flips between kernels across runs and causes ~5-12% throughput jitter in our tests.

jordan: attaching yesterday's profiling snapshot that motivated this. note how p99 jumps as kv_miss_rate increases.

# profile-summary run=2026-03-05/seq-512
p50: 16ms
p90: 48ms
p95: 110ms
p99: 320ms
dominant_kernel: attention_cuda_optimized
kv_miss_rate: 11.8%
cpu_gpu_memcpy_wait: 3.9%

alex: question: are these misses from lack of priming or because generator emits correlated new keys at burst boundaries?

maria: correlated. our current key picker is uniform random which underestimates locality. proposal: use Zipf for key popularity + session affinity so bursts hit new key families then decay.

deepak: also add a `kv-probe-only` mode that emits single-key probes to exercise the cold-miss codepath without triggering batching effects. helps isolate scheduling / memcpy stalls.

alex: rough generator config prototype:
```
generator:
  seed: 20260305
  duration_s: 900
  stages:
    - name: cold_spike
      qps: 1000
      duration_s: 30
      key_dist: zipf(s=1.3)
      session_affinity: 0.9
    - name: mid_tail
      qps: 250
      duration_s: 540
      key_dist: zipf(s=1.05)
      session_affinity: 0.6
    - name: burst_mix
      pattern: poisson_mixture
      avg_qps: 700
      burst_probability: 0.15
      duration_s: 330
  kv_probe_fraction: 0.015
  per_shard_warmup_s: 40
  kernel_pin: [attention_cuda_v2, matmul_tuned_v3]
  quant_modes: [int8_static]
```

jordan: couple of measurement notes:
- keep kv_probe_fraction low for long runs to avoid inflating miss counts
- collect per-shard metrics: kv_miss_rate, kv_lookup_latency_ms, kv_warmup_latency_ms

perfbot: perfbot: CI run compared to baseline 2026-02-28
Regression: p99 increased by +140ms (baseline 180ms -> current 320ms) for seq-512. Likely contributors: higher kv_miss_rate + kernel selection variance.

maria: can we automate a kernel-pin vs kernel-autotune pair run so the harness reports kernel_noise_delta? if we do paired runs with same seed this will make comparisons clearer.

deepak: yes. harness should snapshot env hashes (cuda_driver, cudnn, kernel_versions, libnccl) and persist them with each run so CI can filter noisy infra changes.

alex: action items:
- implement generator stages + Zipf + session affinity (owner: maria)
- add paired kernel-pin vs autotune experiment and env hash capture (owner: deepak)
- add per-shard warmup telemetry to runtime agents (owner: jordan)
- schedule nightly baseline runs and automated comparisons (owner: eng-runtime)

jordan: i'll draft a small analysis notebook that plots p50/p90/p95/p99 vs kv_miss_rate and kernel_set. will link when ready.

maria: small follow-up: include a short `kv_probe_only` experiment in PR so reviewers can run the cold-path microbench without full traffic; helps isolate memcpy / thread scheduling stalls.

alex: agreed. let's run a focused experiment first: 30s cold spike -> 5m steady tail, pinned-kernel vs autotune, deterministic seed. target reproducible baseline by EOD Friday.

perfbot: tagging `#eng-runtime` for CI noise tracking. <https://ci.internal/reports/run/2026-03-05>

maria: ack. i'll open the PR with the generator and example configs. thanks everyone :rocket:
